evidence: PDF pp.3–4, Section 2/3, Equations 2–5/Table 1: Qwen3-8B non-thinking prompts are behaviorally retained for execution-call/analysis-text contrast. The L24 block-input prediction-position mean difference is fitted on 300 pairs; addition/removal flip all 200 held-out pairs in the primary test. Sufficiency 1.03 and necessity 1.04 are normalized logit-gap effects, not probabilities or a universal theorem.

PDF pp.16–18, Tables 7–10/Appendix A: each of seven models has 300 training and 200 held-out pairs. Qwen3.5-4B and Mistral-Small-3.2-24B use Telecom conversation contexts for discovery; the other five use coding tasks. Vectors and native call tokens are model-specific, so there is no single cross-model vector or seven-way coding-only transfer test.

PDF p.5 Table 2 and p.35 Appendix I.1: web retrieval, SQL and email each have 100 held-out pairs; Qwen3-8B induction/suppression are 100% with norm-matched random direction causing no flips. The direction is fixed but its norm is calibrated from disjoint target-domain training pairs; this is not calibration-free transfer.

PDF pp.5–6 and p.19 Tables 3/12/13: native Qwen3-8B Telecom contexts span 5,385–15,690 tokens and 16–43 tools. Removal suppresses 73 of 199 baseline-positive calls (36.7%); all 200 candidates change from 99.5% to 63.0% call rate. Addition induces 140/200 baseline text turns (70%); random controls are 1.5%/0%. These denominators are explicitly reconciled, not conflicting.

PDF p.20 Appendix C.2/Table 14: 600 non-imperative requests are constructed across four domains and five patterns; up to ten baseline-positive requests per cell are retained in source order. Qwen3-8B evaluates 160, with 93.1% suppression at unit gain and 100% at 1.5 versus random 16.2% at 1.5. This is conditional suppression on selected positive cases, not a success rate over all 600 or all natural requests.

PDF pp.6,20–21 Tables 4/15–17: full scaffold neutral/analysis mean call probabilities are .8486/.0038; format alone gives 1.0000/.9952, and removing format nearly eliminates calls. The Review verb produces 4% calls with write_file but 100% with submit_review, supporting request-tool interaction rather than a context-free analysis-verb ban.

PDF pp.7–8,22–23 Figure 4/Tables 5/19/20: MLPs supply 77.7% of projected formation-window writes, analysis-higher absolute feature mass exceeds execution-higher by 1.99 overall. Semantic labels cover 426 of 640 selected candidates; 214 remain unlabelled but are included in full-feature accounting. Absolute mass ratios and semantic labeling do not by themselves establish a complete causal circuit.

PDF p.8 Section 5.3 versus p.23 Appendix D.5, both visually inspected: the same described five-suppressor intervention has post-call rate 25.5% and projection shift +5.30, but main text says baseline 3.0% and strict recovery 45/200 (22.5%), while appendix says baseline 0/200 and strict recovery 51/200 (25.5%). No explicit cohort reconciliation is supplied for this conflict; neither exact recovery value is adopted as definitive.

PDF p.23 Table 21: after swapping L20–23 MLP outputs, execution call rate is already 93% (from 100%) despite projection gap dropping 60.06→15.78; restoring the vector projection returns 100%. Reverse analysis arm rises 0→95% and returns to 0 after restoration. This is asymmetric mediation evidence, not complete removal of execution behavior by the formation swap.

PDF pp.8–9,24–26 Figure 5/Tables 22–26: L33H29 DLA differs across explicitly distinct 300-pair and 200-pair cohorts (7.91 versus 13.45 delta). MLP34 sweep, patching-subset and feature-evaluation call rates (53.3%,42.5%,41.0%) are separately documented and should not be treated as contradictory. On the same feature cohort, F109925 replacement gives 37%, fixed F91365 control 6.5%, full MLP34 41% and vector addition 100%.

PDF pp.21–22,27–29 Appendix D.3/F.2/Figure 6: single-RMSNorm final Qwen3-8B logit gap is 7.093, while cross-model diagnostics apply final RMSNorm twice to the already normalized final hidden state, yielding nominal 14.030. The paper explicitly discloses this; the latter is not an ordinary final model-output logit gap. Early linear separability at L0/L1 is distinguished from later output-space effects and causal interventions.

PDF p.19 Table 11 and p.26 Appendix E.4: Table 11 reports zero execution call rate after L24 subtraction in the independently refitted neighboring-layer control. E.4 cites that N=300 control but reports 1.78% residual calling, without clarifying a different fitted direction/denominator; 1.78% is not an integer single-pass count out of 300. Its separate 0.99% description of 5/500 is also arithmetically imprecise. Keep these auxiliary estimates unresolved rather than merging protocols.

PDF pp.9,19–20,27,29 Tables 6/12–14/27–30: full-state recovery is 93.5–100%, but native induction ranges 7.5–92% and Granite unit-gain verb-free suppression is 35.5%. Kcorrupt/Kclean remains above one across models. Reported transfer regularities coexist with substantial model-specific variation.

PDF pp.30–32 Tables 31/32 and Figures 7/8: Qwen3-8B sparse core replay 1.0000 sufficiency is close to random-core .9768, and EAP-IG needs 100,000 edges for .809 normalized faithfulness. Authors correctly avoid treating sparse-core replay as proof of a unique privileged route; the dense feature graph is an illustrative local attribution view.

PDF p.10 Limitations and pp.35–36 Appendix I: no tests of tool choice, arguments or task completion; implicit-request transfer does not establish identical formation. Code https://github.com/XijieGo/MI4ToolCalling and Hugging Face dataset/checkpoint links are supplied, with about 800 B200 GPU-hours for Transcoder training and a claimed 96GB-GPU reproduction path. Those linked assets were not downloaded, verified or executed in this review.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A relevant and comparatively rich mechanistic study: local addition/subtraction, random directions, scaffold ablations, request-tool crossover, feature mediation and seven-model transfer go beyond correlational probing. The supported conclusion is a reusable model-specific intervention direction for a first-token call marker. Behaviorally screened prompts and norm-calibrated cross-domain tests do not establish an unconditional universal switch, identical formation on implicit requests, or improved downstream task success. The main-text versus appendix suppressor-ablation baseline/strict-recovery conflict remains unresolved; diagnostic double-normalization and an ambiguous neighboring-control result require careful separation. These reporting limitations reduce evidence confidence without making the complete supplied PDF a missing-source case.

llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這是高度相關且證據面較豐富的機制研究：局部加減向量、隨機方向、提示結構消融、請求與工具交叉、中介介入及七模型遷移，超越單純相關探測。較穩健的結論是，各模型存在可重用的首詞元工具呼叫介入方向。經行為篩選的提示與跨領域長度校準，不能證明無條件通用開關、隱含請求具有完全相同的形成機制，或下游任務成功率提升。正文及附錄對抑制特徵消融的基線／嚴格復原率有未解衝突，診斷雙重正規化與鄰層控制結果的指涉亦應分開。這些論文報告限制降低證據信心，但不代表已取得的完整 PDF 有缺件。

primary_link.title: How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? A Tool-Call Vector Shaped by Suppression

papers.summary: Tool calling, invoking external tools on demand, is central to agentic LLMs, yet the mechanism that decides whether a model calls a tool or responds directly remains poorly understood. Agentic prompts are long and heavily scaffolded, combining role instructions, tool schemas, format templates, and the user's request across hundreds of tokens, creating a noisy, highly entangled context in which no single controllable variable for mechanistic analysis is obvious. To obtain such a variable, we propose a method that converts complex agentic prompts into minimal contrastive pairs in which a single request verb determines the tool-call decision: replacing an execution-verb (e.g., \textit{write}) with an analysis-verb (e.g., \textit{discuss}) reliably flips the decision, suggesting it is mediated by a compact internal state. We construct 500 such paired prompts across Python, Java, and C++ (300 for mechanistic analysis, 200 held out for evaluation). We trace the decision to a vector, $\mu_\Delta$, that is both causally necessary and sufficient and generalizes beyond the discovery prompts to native multi-turn $\tau^2$-Bench trajectories and verb-free requests. Behavioral ablations show that the scaffold establishes a tool-call prior; Transcoder decomposition then reveals that analysis verbs suppress this prior through features signaling that tool use is unnecessary, whereas execution verbs largely leave it intact. Downstream scaffold-reading attention heads and MLP features read out the resulting state, and the same mechanism recurs across seven models from the Qwen, Mistral, and Granite families. Our code is available at https://github.com/XijieGo/MI4ToolCalling.
papers.summary_en: A residual vector fitted from verb-swapped prompts can flip Qwen3-8B's first tool-call token. Scaffold ablations and feature interventions support a suppression-based account, with tests across seven models and native dialogues. Yet native Qwen3-8B calls are suppressed only 36.7% at unit gain; task success is untested and cross-domain transfer calibrates vector norm. Main-text and appendix suppressor-ablation rates conflict. All 36 pages, figures and tables were read; linked code and checkpoints were not rerun.
papers.summary_zh:
一句請求中的動詞，可能改變代理選擇直接回答還是呼叫工具。這篇研究先篩出只替換動詞就能翻轉首個輸出詞元的成對提示，主要以 Qwen3-8B 的三百組資料估計中間層活化差向量，再用二百組保留資料測試。加上或減去此向量，可在受控提示中完全翻轉工具呼叫標記。

分析指出，工具格式範本先建立呼叫傾向，要求討論、分析的語意則透過多層 MLP 特徵壓低傾向；後段注意力與 MLP 再將狀態轉成輸出。它不是單一神經元開關，也不是跨模型共用同一組向量。研究涵蓋七個模型，並測試新工具、長對話及沒有明示動作動詞的請求。在原生 τ²-Bench 對話中，Qwen3-8B 的單位強度介入抑制 36.7% 既有呼叫，誘發 70% 原本直接回答的回合，效果遠非一律百分之百。

重要限制是只判斷首詞元，沒有驗證工具選擇、參數或任務完成；跨領域結果還校準了向量長度。正文與附錄對五項抑制特徵消融的起始呼叫率及嚴格復原率存在矛盾，不能合併引用。三十六頁、八圖與三十三表已讀，程式、資料與 Transcoder 連結有列出但未重跑。其價值在可介入的機制線索，尚不能當作通用可靠性或安全控制。

links.title: SkillSandbox: Skill Verification via Dynamic Scenario Synthesis

evidence: PDF pp.4–5, Section 3 and Figure 2: Proposer preserves applicability conditions while varying context, Builder constructs executable scenarios and obtains five valid scenarios per skill, and Verifier uses paired trajectories with and without the skill; keep iff empirical score is positive.

PDF p.6, Table 2 and implementation details: three executors, same 100 source tasks, frozen libraries; evaluation uses 140 ALFWorld and 500 WebShop tasks. Qwen3.5-27B WebShop SR is 32.2% No Skill versus 45.0% SkillSandbox, a derived 12.8 percentage-point gain; mean steps 8.0 versus 7.2. ACE reaches 37.4%, so gain over that stronger baseline is 7.6 points, not 12.8.

PDF pp.7–8, Section 5.1/Figure 3: same Verifier and five-scenario/execution/task budget compares synthesized, source and random evidence. Gemini-labelled executor ALFWorld SR is 60.0% synthesized versus 50.7% source and 44.3% random; WebShop is 36.2% versus 33.0% and 31.6%.

PDF p.8, Table 3: Gemini 3.1 Flash-labelled Proposer gives WebShop precision/recall/F1/specificity 96.0/82.8/88.9/94.4%, versus ALFWorld 39.1/81.8/52.9/60.0%. Section 4.1 says Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is used for execution, synthesis and verification; Tables 1/3/6 use Flash. This discrepancy is retained rather than silently normalized.

PDF pp.3 and 15: Figure 1 reports mean and one-standard-deviation bands from three repeats of one fixed 500-task stream, based on self-cited skill IDs. This uncertainty evidence does not apply to the main results in Table 2, and cited use is not causal verification of actual skill reliance.

PDF pp.14–15, Appendices A/B: ReasoningBank excludes MaTTS, MemP uses Script/Vanilla, SkillOS uses training-free base; ACE receives the whole playbook, unlike common top-three retrieval. Alignment uses identical observations, temporally ordered one-to-one pairs and discount 0<gamma<1, but a numeric gamma and empty-alignment handling are not supplied.

PDF pp.9 and 16–18, Figures 4–6/Tables 5–7: success and action efficiency can disagree; WebShop both-success skill pairs take extra actions. Rejected-skill cases illustrate overgeneralized appliance ordering and needless two-section verification. Synthesis type shares overlap and must not be summed as mutually exclusive categories.

PDF pp.17–18, Table 7: k=3 is selected after reporting the highest held-out SR (84/140 and 181/500). A distinct tuning/validation split is not described, so possible held-out selection bias is a limitation, not proven data leakage.

PDF p.2 promises omission-of-executability/efficiency ablations and larger gains on unseen task types. Full reading of pp.1–22, all six figures and seven tables found no corresponding displayed component-ablation or held-out-task-type results; these claims are not credited.

PDF pp.19–22, Appendix F: execution and distillation templates are included, but Proposer prompts are summaries and retry/format-repair messages are omitted. The first-page CODE hyperlink is https://anonymous.4open.science/r/skillsandbox-647C/; its target was not inspected or executed.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strong fit for agent skill and memory curation, with an actionable distinction between a skill-relevant test and a merely similar task. Frozen-library held-out tests and a matched verification-rollout comparison support the scenario-synthesis contribution. However, ALFWorld verdict precision is only 39.1% for the Gemini-labelled row; main tables lack uncertainty and do not include construction cost. Restricted baseline variants, Flash versus Flash-Lite labels, unspecified discount settings and introductory ablation/unseen-task claims without displayed results limit confidence. Evidence supports this bounded filtering approach, not universal skill verification, model independence or net compute savings.

llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這篇與代理技能及記憶管理高度相關，清楚區分真正會觸發技能的測試與僅語意相似的任務。凍結技能庫的保留測試，以及驗證回合預算相同的比較，支持情境合成的貢獻。然而 Gemini 標籤列在 ALFWorld 的技能判決精確率只有 39.1%；主要結果缺乏不確定性，亦未計入建構成本。基線受限版本、Flash 與 Flash-Lite 名稱差異、未指定折扣，以及導論宣稱卻未展示的消融與未見任務結果，皆限制可信度。證據支持特定環境內的篩選方法，不支持通用技能保證、模型能力無關性或整體運算節省。
llm_evaluation.scope_assessment: In scope: reusable textual skill verification for language agents operating in text-action environments; ALFWorld is a language-agent benchmark, not a claim of physical robotics performance.

primary_link.title: SkillSandbox: Skill Verification via Dynamic Scenario Synthesis

papers.summary: Self-evolving agents distill task-solving experience into skills for future reuse, but these skills can encode incorrect procedures or non-transferable knowledge. It is therefore critical to verify each skill's reusability: whether its guidance remains useful beyond the experience from which it was distilled. Such verification requires observing how a skill affects execution in new tasks, yet existing tasks may not expose the situations where the target skill can actually be exercised. To construct such situations, we propose SkillSandbox, a framework that dynamically synthesizes a task and its environment for each skill that are skill-relevant yet novel. A Proposer specifies the conditions to preserve and the source-specific details to vary, a Builder constructs an executable scenario, and a Verifier compares executions with and without the skill. The Verifier assesses executability, utility, and efficiency to assign a Keep or Reject verdict, determining whether the skill enters the library. Across ALFWorld and WebShop with three models, SkillSandbox consistently yields the strongest downstream performance and improved execution efficiency. Further analyses examine whether these gains reflect accurate assessment of skill reusability and identify which components of SkillSandbox contribute to them.
papers.summary_en: SkillSandbox creates new executable scenarios for each skill, then compares an agent with and without it before library admission. Qwen3.5-27B improves WebShop success from 32.2% to 45.0%; downstream steps exclude synthesis costs. Read the matched-budget comparison and failure cases, but note weak ALFWorld verdict precision, missing uncertainty, model-label inconsistencies and unshown introductory ablation claims. All 22 pages were read; the linked code was not inspected and results were not reproduced.
papers.summary_zh:
代理把一次成功經驗存成技能，可能連當時偶然有效的做法也一起記住。SkillSandbox 針對每項技能主動建立新測試：提案者保留技能適用條件、改動原任務細節，建構器生成可執行情境，再比較同一代理使用與不使用技能的軌跡。評分兼顧動作可執行性、成功結果與剩餘步數，只有正分技能進入資料庫。

作者以相同的一百項來源任務建立各方法的技能庫，固定後測試 ALFWorld 一百四十題及 WebShop 五百題。Qwen3.5-27B 在 WebShop 的成功率由無技能的 32.2% 升至 45.0%，平均步數由 8.0 降至 7.2；這些步數只涵蓋下游作答，不能當成合成與驗證也更省。固定驗證回合預算的比較支持合成情境，但技能判定品質依環境差很多，不能把保留判決當成安全或可移轉保證。

閱讀時宜先看成對比較和錯誤案例，再檢查代價與基線設定。主要結果沒有信賴區間，部分基線採簡化版本；表格中的 Gemini 名稱與實作段落不一致，折扣參數也未給定。導論另外宣稱的逐項判準消融與未見任務類型結果，現有正文及附錄未展示。完整二十二頁與圖表已讀，程式連結未另行驗證；目前證據支持技能庫篩選方法，尚不足以外推到開放網頁、真實機器人或任意模型。

links.title: SkillForge: Co-Evolving Skills and Agents via Dynamic Skill Lifecycles

evidence: PDF pp.3–6, Equations 2–12 and Algorithm 1: task-type matching retrieves top-K skills; pre-retirement removes skills with low base-policy success; successful trajectories involving surviving skills seed SFT. Runtime tracks trial/active/stable/retired states and uses a distinct teacher family for mutation.

PDF pp.5–6 and p.16 Table 6: K=6 retrieved skills all receive the same binary episode reward; cumulative success/usage drives lifecycle. Default retirement/demotion/stability thresholds are .4/.5/.7, with at most 5 mutations and 3 ordinary retirements per 10 training steps.

PDF pp.7–8 Table 2/Section 5.2: SkillForge reports ALFWorld 92.4 and WebShop 78.4 success versus SkillRL 89.9/72.7. WebShop improvement is 5.7 percentage points or about 7.84% relative, not 7.8 percentage points.

PDF p.7 Table 2 and p.15 Appendix B: ALFWorld subtask counts are 24,15,27,26,21,17 and SkillForge rates 98.2,86.6,89.8,93.7,95.6,88.4. Their sample-weighted mean is 92.5153846%, whereas All is 92.4%; the discrepancy exceeds ordinary one-decimal rounding allowance. SkillRL recomputes to 89.8738462%, compatible with 89.9. Values were checked in rendered pages; raw outputs are unavailable to resolve the difference.

PDF p.8 Table 3: removing pre-retirement lowers success by 1.7/3.5/1.2 points, retirement by 1.0/2.5/.8 and mutation by .6/1.6/.5 across ALFWorld/WebShop/QA. These component ablations support contribution but do not isolate individual-skill causal harm.

PDF pp.15–17 Tables 5–7: one Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct policy, Kimi-K2.5 teacher, 200 steps, learning rate 1e-6, 64 H200 GPUs; reported training cost totals 7,296 GPU-hours across three environments plus pre-retirement/evaluation. ALFWorld retirement/cap sweeps stay within 1.4 points of default.

PDF pp.19–20 Appendix D/Table 10: 51,713 QA samples, two in-domain and five out-of-domain datasets; other methods' cells are imported from source papers. Displayed rates recompute to SkillForge 48.6529 and SkillRL 46.8243, compatible with 48.7/46.8, but common weighting does not establish identical original evaluation conditions.

PDF pp.5,17–20 Tables 1/8/9 and Figures 3–7: 5,852 records comprise 1,013 SFT trajectories, 4,521 per-skill snapshots and 318 retirement events aggregated over several runs. They are not 5,852 independent tasks/skills. The main run has 84 retirements; 318 aggregate events are explicitly explained, not a count contradiction.

PDF pp.20–21 Appendix E.2/Figure 7: two annotators initially achieve Cohen kappa .5 before discussion; 237/318 events are labeled overly rigid ordering, and 57.2% of retired skills reportedly reached stable state earlier. Annotation and declining conditional success support a descriptive failure taxonomy, not counterfactual proof that each skill caused failure.

PDF pp.6,21–23: Algorithm 1 caps only by removing active skills and can stop above cap if none remain; trial children are inserted into the non-retired library. Therefore a universal hard-size guarantee and a claim that trial gating prevents any influence before active status are not established by the presented algorithm. Appendix H also says the no-mutation library values refer to initial |S0|, while Table 3 labels them final counts.

PDF p.24 Appendix H: every number averages five decoding-seed evaluations of the best validation checkpoint; reported SDs are .5/.4/.3 points. One-sample t-tests compare against fixed SkillRL point estimates; the Welch alternative assumes baseline variance equal to SkillForge's rather than measuring it. This does not establish independently trained-run variance or matched-baseline uncertainty.

PDF pp.17–19 describes a CC-BY-4.0 SkillFurnace release with three JSON files and a schema. All 24 pages, references, appendices A–H, ten tables and seven figures were read; neither text nor PDF URI annotations contained a direct SkillForge/SkillFurnace download link. No author code, external dataset or experiment was retrieved or executed.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A highly relevant skill-memory/RL contribution with useful lifecycle controls, three-environment ablations, threshold sensitivity and failure-taxonomy analysis. The scientific case is promising but not definitive: co-retrieved skills share reward, cumulative fitness is not a causal estimate of skill harm, baseline QA scores come from separate papers, and five stochastic evaluations of a selected checkpoint do not establish training-seed robustness. The one-sample significance analysis ignores observed baseline uncertainty; the subsequent Welch calculation assumes rather than measures it. A small ALFWorld weighted-aggregate discrepancy and lifecycle-description ambiguities require explicit qualification. The complete PDF is available; these are reporting and evidential limitations, not missing-source holds. Claimed dataset availability remains unverified.

primary_link.title: SkillForge: Co-Evolving Skills and Agents via Dynamic Skill Lifecycles

papers.summary: Memory-augmented reinforcement learning strengthens LLM agents' ability to solve complex long-horizon tasks. Skills are one such form of memory, pairing instructions with an applicability condition over task types. However, retaining every skill indiscriminately as the policy improves lets obsolete or harmful entries accumulate and mislead the agent. We propose SkillForge, an agentic RL method that compiles and evolves the skill library through a fitness-driven skill lifecycle of trial, active, stable, and retired states, so that the skills and the model co-evolve throughout training. A pre-RL evaluation phase first uses the base model's own rollouts to pre-retire low-fitness skills, yielding a filtered library that then seeds supervised fine-tuning. Reinforcement learning takes over from this checkpoint, and at each iteration selective retirement, stabilization, and LLM-guided mutation continue to forge the skill library alongside policy optimization. Across multiple interactive agent benchmarks, SkillForge achieves the highest aggregate success rate, delivering up to 7.8% relative improvement over the strongest baseline while keeping the skill library compact throughout training. We introduce SkillFurnace, a dataset of 5k+ annotated records bundling retirement-filtered SFT trajectories, evolved skill libraries with fitness annotations, and retirement events with human-annotated failure categories to support research on skill quality and lifecycle management.

Reported WebShop success rises from 72.7% to 78.4%; ablations support filtering and lifecycle management. Shared episode rewards cannot isolate individual skill effects, five evaluation seeds do not establish training robustness, and imported QA baselines weaken comparability. A small ALFWorld aggregation discrepancy remains. All 24 pages and figures were read; the claimed dataset release was not verified.

primary_link.title: RewardWeaver: Long-Horizon Interactive Learning for Language Agents via Self-Evolving Reward Adaptation

papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has driven substantial progress in domains where task outcomes can be reliably evaluated, but long-horizon interaction remains challenging due to sparse terminal feedback and difficult credit assignment. Process rewards provide denser supervision, yet the capabilities most relevant for training can change as the policy evolves: a behavior that is easy to evaluate or frequently deficient need not be the bottleneck currently limiting task success. We introduce RewardWeaver, a self-evolving reward adaptation framework for language agents in long-horizon interaction. RewardWeaver maintains a validated capability space in which the semantics of admitted Rubrics remain fixed, and closes the loop between policy optimization, task evaluation, failure attribution, and reward adaptation. After each training stage, it performs outcome-grounded backward attribution on low-outcome trajectories, aggregates recurrent and policy-controlled capability bottlenecks, and dynamically selects the corresponding process rewards for the next stage. Recurrent failures not covered by the existing capability space trigger a separate, controlled expansion procedure. We evaluate REWARDWEAVER on SOTOPIA, Amazon?HistoryPrice, and a newly constructed Sales Benchmark. Across social interaction, bilateral bargaining, and domain-specific sales, REWARDWEAVER establishes new state-of-the-art (SOTA) results. Ablations further demonstrate the importance of dynamic reward allocation, failure-grounded attribution, and stable semantics for admitted capabilities.
papers.summary_en: RewardWeaver changes which process rewards a dialogue agent optimizes while freezing admitted rubric meanings. Failure-grounded selection beats matched alternatives on several benchmarks, but Sales wins six of eight metrics. Read the ablations before accepting broad SOTA claims: literature partners differ, Sales tests share scenario families with training, and uncertainty and implementation details are limited. All 23 pages and figures were reviewed; experiments and promised release materials were not independently verified.
papers.summary_zh:
多輪對話代理即使知道最後失敗，也未必知道下一階段應改善什麼。RewardWeaver 把這個問題拆成兩層：內層用強化學習更新策略，外層從低成果對話找出反覆出現、且由代理自身控制的能力缺口，再挑選相應的過程獎勵。已接納的評分規則與評分器維持固定；新能力須另外驗證，延後到後續階段使用，避免訓練目標隨意漂移。

作者在社交互動、議價與合成銷售情境評估。SOTOPIA-Hard 自我對弈中，相同設定的 AMPO 目標／整體分數為 7.67／3.94，本方法為 7.90／4.38；隨機換規則與只按缺陷頻率選擇的消融較弱，支持有根據的動態選擇。銷售基準則只在八項指標中的六項最佳，並非全面勝出。

閱讀時要留意比較邊界：舊文獻的對手與本次實驗不同，不能把整張表視為完全公平的排行榜。銷售測試與訓練共享情境家族與人物設定庫，僅衡量家族內新任務；論文未給多種隨機種子的變異、信賴區間或完整訓練與評分器驗收參數。完整二十三頁及附錄已核對，但未重現實驗，也未查證承諾發布的資料與程式。它值得作為獎勵設計方法閱讀，成果仍受模型評分器、任務範圍與重現資訊限制。

primary_link.title: Loud Failures, Quiet Failures: Fault Detection and Recovery in Tool-Using Language Model Agents

papers.summary: Tool-using agents are usually scored on whether they finish a task while the tools work. Deployments are less forgiving: services time out, endpoints disappear, parameter names change, and results come back well formed but wrong. Prior work has shown that language models over-trust tool outputs that fail silently; we ask how that over-trust plays out across the stages of failure handling in multi-turn agents. Wrapping the executable environments of an established function-calling benchmark in a fault-injection layer, we inject one of four typed faults at a controlled point in the trajectory and record whether the agent notices, changes plan, recovers the task, or repeats itself. Six models from three families, half of them reasoning variants, ran 1,920 trials over 24 multi-step tasks. Agents treat a failure as a problem in 91.3% of trials when the tool returns an explicit error, but in 58.8% of trials when it returns a plausible wrong value, against a 26.8% rate of reporting problems when nothing was wrong. Reasoning models are not better placed: paired against instruct siblings, they notice less (-9.3 points, p < .001) and change plan more (+10.4 points, p < .001), and recovery is unchanged (p = .512). Because agents are stochastic, two fault-free runs of the same task end in the same state only 63.3% of the time; against that baseline, only a missing tool clearly lowers recovery (39.9%), while timeouts, schema drift, and corruption stay within run-to-run variation. After a fault, agents return to the same tool three or more times in a row in up to 22.2% of trials, though strictly identical repeats are rare. A prompt line asking the agent to check each result did not move detection. Agents respond to the error channel rather than to the content of what a tool returns, so failures that stay inside the expected format pass through.
papers.summary_en: This study separates fault detection, replanning, end-state recovery and repetition in tool agents. Table IV reports 91.3% detection for explicit errors versus 58.8% for silent corruption, but Figure 1 shows different rates and sample counts. Recovery matches a model's own clean-run state, not ground-truth task success. Task-clustered analyses are useful, yet 24 tasks, three model pairs and textual detection limit transfer. All eight pages were read; the numerical conflict remains and data were not recomputed.
papers.summary_zh:
工具沒有報錯，不代表回傳內容可信。這篇研究在 BFCL 的可執行多輪環境注入逾時、工具缺失、參數變動與格式正常但內容錯誤的回傳，分開量測代理是否表達懷疑、是否改變下一步、是否回到正常執行的終態，以及是否重複呼叫。六個模型在二十四項任務執行一千九百二十次，扣除未觸發故障的試驗後分析一千六百九十四次。

表四與正文報告，明顯錯誤的偵測率為 91.3%，靜默錯誤為 58.8%；但同頁圖一卻標成 86% 與 53%，樣本數也不同，因此精確比例仍有未解矛盾，不能把圖表說成相互驗證。研究較有價值的是拆開失敗處理階段：推理版本較常改變行動，不代表更常察覺錯誤；其復原差異未達顯著，也不是證明兩者等效。

尤其要注意，這裡的復原指與同模型一次無故障執行的環境終態一致，並非達成標準答案。錯誤資訊可能被帶進回覆，卻不改變環境狀態。研究提供任務分群統計與人工標註一致性檢查，但只有三組模型、單一基準家族、十五次工具呼叫上限，且偵測依文字表達判定。八頁正文和全部圖表已核對，連結資料未重算；適合借鏡其測試設計，對精確數值、模型優劣及部署安全結論則需保留。

radar.summary:
This Japanese architecture article asks whether an application can safely execute tool calls together, rather than merely whether a model can emit several calls at once. It separates tool selection from execution order: independent reads can run concurrently, while writes require checks of dependencies, target resources and retry semantics. Valid JSON arguments establish structure, not transactional consistency between order creation and inventory updates.

A timeout-and-retry example illustrates duplicate orders. The proposed design assigns a stable idempotency key to a logical operation before invoking the LLM, then uses a dependency graph to release executable nodes. The small Python example only gathers reads and awaits writes one by one. The author acknowledges that it still trusts input-array order and is not a complete scheduler. Writes may also run concurrently when a lower service provides an atomic transaction or the application guarantees nonconflict.

The article is a useful executor-design checklist, not a validated safety or speed solution. Its stock-decrement example is labeled idempotent without durable deduplication, and results do not retain tool-call identifiers. Authorization, locking, error handling and fault tests remain necessary. No benchmark or production measurements are provided; the illustrations are conceptual and cannot establish a reliability gain.

https://qiita.com/hono_ai_labho/items/2560290ec993ec7be189 | section ログと検証ポイント, [5496,6268): displays assertions for 503/503/200 and immediate 401 failure, but mock_server and call_llm definitions are absent; no complete test output, benchmark or measured reliability improvement is provided. HTTPX official timeout documentation, Fine tuning the configuration: read timeout is a per-chunk wait, not a total call deadline (https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/timeouts/). RFC 9110 section 10.2.3 permits either HTTP-date or delay-seconds for Retry-After (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-10.2.3). These primary references corroborate the identified implementation limitations.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Relevant to LLM application serving and reliability engineering, but this is a practical blog tutorial rather than peer-reviewed research or a new LLM method. Error classification, bounded retries, jitter, idempotency cautions, and a local token bucket are useful established ideas. The author reports informal mock testing without a complete fixture, helper implementation, measured reliability gains, baselines, load study, or uncertainty. Independent isolated checks confirm the displayed success/error branches but expose material gaps: a successful call can return after the claimed 90-second overall deadline; Retry-After HTTP-date values fall back to one second; and retries bypass the separately acquired token bucket despite the flowchart returning through it. Exhausted HTTP-error retries also sleep after the final attempt. The readable code supports reproduction of these control-flow checks, not production reliability claims. Research novelty and evidential rigor are low, and the example needs corrections before operational reuse.

radar.summary: This implementation tutorial outlines reliability measures for calling LLM APIs: distinguishing temporary failures from authentication or input errors, configuring connection and read/write timeouts, retrying with exponential backoff and jitter, and limiting request frequency with a local token bucket. It also warns that resubmission can duplicate charges or external effects and recommends logging attempts, waiting time, and failure reasons without exposing keys or full prompts. Its evidence consists mainly of code fragments and informal accounts of mock testing, without a complete test environment, performance measurements, or reliability comparisons. Independent offline checks find that the overall deadline is checked only between attempts and cannot prevent a request from returning success after expiry. A server waiting header in date format is not parsed correctly. The token bucket is acquired only before the whole application call, so internal retries do not pass through it again, contrary to the flowchart; an extra wait can also follow the last failure. These are control-flow checks, not measurements of a real provider. Read the article as a reliability checklist, but correct deadline handling, waiting-header parsing, and per-attempt rate limiting, and supply executable tests before assessing production use. Multiple processes and hosts also require shared rate-limit state rather than relying directly on the in-memory implementation.
radar.summary_zh: 這篇實作教學整理呼叫大型語言模型 API 時的可靠性設計，包括區分暫時故障與認證或輸入錯誤、設定連線及讀寫逾時、以指數退避加隨機抖動重試，以及使用本機令牌桶限制請求頻率。作者也提醒重送可能造成重複計費或外部副作用，並建議記錄嘗試次數、等待時間與失敗原因，避免洩漏金鑰與完整提示。其證據主要是程式片段與非正式模擬測試敘述，沒有完整測試環境、效能量測或可靠性比較。獨立離線檢查發現，總期限只在嘗試之間檢查，無法阻止請求超時後仍回傳成功；服務端等待標頭若採日期格式，程式也未正確解析。令牌桶只在整個呼叫前取得一次，內部重試不會再次限流，與流程圖不一致；最後一次失敗後還可能多做等待。這些是程式控制流程的檢查結果，並非真實供應商測速。閱讀時可把本文當成可靠性設計清單，但應先修正期限控制、等待標頭處理及逐次限流，補齊可執行的測試，再評估生產使用。多程序與跨主機情境亦需共享限流狀態，不能直接依賴本機記憶體實作。

Vendor benchmarks and a single-run case are starting points for testing, not grounds for directly following the table or expecting universal savings.

radar.summary: This article addresses the gap between generating an LLM action proposal and safely executing consequential operations. It separates proposal from execution: store the action, arguments and reason, then let the server enforce approval-state requirements. A Python/FastAPI in-memory example distinguishes pending, approved, rejected, executed and failed states and illustrates routing by action risk, recipient and content. Its practical value is locating human decision points within tool-use workflows rather than letting the model declare an action safe. Evidence consists only of snippets and operating steps: model output is fixed, email sending only prints, and no real model, mail service or deployment test is provided. The minimal code lacks authentication, atomic transitions and idempotency, so it does not establish protection against concurrent duplicate execution. Content hashes, authorization, idempotency, expiry and audit records are recommended production additions, not existing guarantees. Readers can reuse the architectural separation and responsibility boundaries, but should not treat the tutorial as experimental evidence of safety or efficiency gains. All nodes, labels and transitions in the embedded state diagram were checked; rendered pixels and historical-version completeness were not verified.

radar.summary: This practitioner article addresses vague metaphors, missing agents and unnatural collocations in Japanese generated text. Its aim is to flag sentences for rereading, not determine AI authorship. The author supplies paragraph context for each sentence, asks Jev six types of style question, and flags candidates using thresholds from 0.35 to 0.5. Claude then rewrites them, while another AI checks comprehension difficulties. Six of eight sentences in a pull-request description were flagged; examples replace vague mouth and footprint metaphors with concrete process and log descriptions and add explicit subjects. The author’s own 47-sentence draft produced 26 candidates, but only six sentences were edited. Nine remaining candidates were quoted examples and 11 were judged acceptable by the author. Candidates therefore still need human review, and the edited fraction is not detector precision. The article acknowledges missed headings and excessive token consumption when checking every response. It offers a reusable proofreading workflow, but no independent annotations, baseline comparisons, threshold calibration or repeated experiments, and omits the full script and model settings. The examples support this author’s limited experience, not a general improvement, reliable AI-text detection or performance equivalence with another service.

radar.summary: This Japanese practitioner blog summarizes nineteen unauthorized-access and data-leak disclosures, including follow-ups, published from September 11 to October 5. It asks whether AI has changed attack techniques or reduced the cost of finding old vulnerabilities. Cases were selected by impact or name recognition, and the author explicitly disclaims statistical representativeness. Six entries mention vulnerabilities and two mention unauthorized logins, but the absence of AI mentions does not establish that attackers did not use AI. Read the incident table and five patterns first, then the separately cited model-capability reports, without joining these two bodies of evidence into a causal chain. The cited sandbox exploit tests and simulated harmful-task engagement rates describe capability under particular conditions; they cannot directly explain these nineteen incidents. Practical priorities are keeping systems updateable, continuously checking code and configuration, and limiting damage through privilege separation, multifactor authentication, logging, backups and data minimization. Impact figures mix people, accounts, records and sent emails, sometimes describing only possible exposure, so they should not be added together. The article is useful for reviewing defensive questions and tracing original announcements. It is neither a new language-model method, a study of AI-attack prevalence nor experimental proof that the proposed defenses work. The author explicitly preserves uncertainty about a causal connection between these incidents and AI.

radar.summary: This article asks how instructions should change as coding agents become more capable. Its central recommendation is that, when an agent can inspect a codebase and compare implementations, people should prioritize context, purpose, constraints, domain knowledge, trade-offs and completion criteria rather than prescribing every file and function. A per-tab search-state example contrasts a storage-specific task list with an outcome-focused request that includes impact analysis and tests; a six-category table organizes the information humans should supply. This is communication and delegation advice, with no evaluated model, version, repository, actual task trace, control group, success rate or timing data. It therefore does not establish that fewer implementation details improve quality or productivity. Nor does the author advocate abandoning supervision: architecture, security, change scope and release decisions must remain explicit or under human control, and tests, reviews, diff inspection and rollback means still matter. Practitioners can use the checklist to assess whether requirements are clear and adjust delegation to the agent’s actual competence; less capable agents still need task decomposition. Its value is distinguishing code-discoverable information from human business judgment, not introducing an algorithm or validated prompt-optimization method. The related-article link was not treated as experimental evidence. Supplied text and table content were checked; historical-version completeness remains unverified.

top5.summary:
This Japanese practitioner report argues that a coding agent’s claim of completed verification should be examined in terms of the user path it actually exercised. The author’s iPhone app was committed after launch-flag transitions, recordings and performance checks, yet crashed on finger scrolling four minutes later. The reported cause was early WebView creation: the recording showed rendered pages without traversing the failing touch-handling path.

The stronger part is the subsequent countercheck. Published commit excerpts and animated session replays show a touch-driven UI test failing on the broken commit, passing on its parent, and passing after repair three times in the simulator and once on hardware. Separate deployment and audit cases illustrate that a running service need not contain the new build, and existing code need not be reachable from the application. The proposed acceptance criteria are sequences of operations, accompanied by output evidence and untested paths.

These are author-selected engineering cases, not a controlled study of agent reliability. The animations are edited replays, and the full repository and original crash records are unavailable for independent reproduction. A changed process ID also does not establish build identity; the actual artifact must be checked. The transferable lesson is to exercise affected paths while choosing checks proportionate to risk and cost. Passing a scrolling test does not establish safety for rotation, pinch or every device, and reasoning self-correction research is not direct causal evidence for this case.
top5.summary_zh:
這篇日文實務紀錄指出，程式代理說「驗證完成」時，必須追問它走過的是哪一條使用路徑。作者的 iPhone 應用程式經啟動旗標切換畫面、錄影與效能檢查後提交，四分鐘後卻在手指捲動時崩潰。問題據報來自過早建立 WebView；錄影看到了已繪製頁面，沒有經過出錯的觸控處理。

較有力的部分是後續反向檢查：作者展示的提交摘錄與工作階段動畫顯示，觸控式 UI 測試在故障提交失敗，在父提交通過，修復後又於模擬器通過三次、實機通過一次。另兩個部署與稽核案例提醒，服務仍在運行不代表新版本已載入，程式碼存在也不代表能從應用程式入口呼叫。文章因此把驗收條件寫成操作序列，要求附上輸出證據及尚未走過的路徑。

這是作者挑選的工程案例，不是代理可靠性的受控研究。公開動畫是刪節重播，沒有完整儲存庫與原始崩潰紀錄可供獨立重現；程序識別碼改變也不足以證明版本正確，仍須核對實際產物。可採用的是讓測試真正經過受影響路徑的原則，同時依風險控制成本。通過捲動測試不代表旋轉、縮放或所有裝置都安全，也不能把推理自我修正的研究直接當成此案例的因果證據。

top5.summary:
This Japanese technical article organizes common causes of Claude prompt-cache misses. Its central lesson is to inspect writes, reads and uncached input separately rather than assuming that cache_control guarantees savings. After examining three personal projects, the author found that a subtitle pipeline logged only its first chunk; its consistently zero read counter therefore could not establish whether later requests hit the cache. A separate paired probe reports cache write/read counts changing from 1123/0 to 0/1123 while uncached input remaining 13.

The article covers variable system prompts, changing tool definitions, length thresholds, breakpoint placement, thinking and effort settings, and expiration. It recommends comparing adjacent requests, inspecting diagnostic fields, and testing whether an identical second request hits the cache. These are primarily explanations of existing mechanisms, not a new caching algorithm.

The evidence is a small set of author observations, without systematic comparisons of cost, latency or hit rate, or data supporting the frequency ordering. Model thresholds and pricing must be checked for the deployed version. Periodic refresh still incurs cache-read and uncached-input charges, and zero-output requests have compatibility limits. Stable tool definitions cannot replace authorization, and request logging requires attention to privacy.

top5.summary: This Japanese design blog separates external memory for long-term ChatGPT use into storage, retrieval and formal adoption. The central idea is not to save more conversation. It is to resolve the project, retrieve required operational rules separately, and then read currently active, relevant memory. New experiences are marked unreviewed and can become formal rules only after a separate evaluation. Start with the flow diagram, then read the minimal Python example and the section on deliberate omissions to distinguish design intent from implemented capability. The public example uses synthetic data and includes nine conformance tests covering project filtering, exclusion of retired records, duplicate writeback and missing gates, among other cases. Static code inspection confirms that these test definitions exist, but no tests were executed in this review, and their existence does not demonstrate improved long-term answer quality. The sample stores data only in memory, checks whether an evidence string is present rather than whether it is true, and cannot recognize semantic duplicates. Project filtering likewise cannot replace authentication and access control. A production system still needs persistence, permissions, auditing, independent verification and failure recovery. The article offers a discussable lifecycle and trust-boundary design; quality, latency, cost and maintenance burden still need controlled comparisons. This is an independent experimental architecture, not an official OpenAI feature or a ready-to-deploy memory product.

top5.summary: This technical explainer discusses a common RAG tuning pitfall: retrieving more items may recover necessary documents while also passing irrelevant material to the language model. The author computes document-level recall and precision for two manually specified FAQ rankings; the example first recovers a missed answer document and then adds only noise. Another code example combines a result-count limit with a score threshold, noting that a high threshold may remove necessary evidence. In practice, hold chunking and ranking settings fixed and use the same labeled questions to track retrieved documents, retrieval metrics, and final answer quality separately. For questions requiring multiple documents, label the complete evidence set and keep adding cases representative of real traffic. Crucially, the article runs neither a real retrieval model nor answer generation, and provides no experiments comparing models, corpora, or thresholds; its two images are conceptual illustrations. It therefore offers reproducible teaching calculations, not proof that increasing result count necessarily reduces answer accuracy. Precision can rise or fall with the relevance of added documents, and scores do not guarantee correctness. Use it to establish diagnostics and small tests, not as a new research result or universal parameter prescription.
top5.summary_zh: 這篇技術解說討論 RAG 常見的調整陷阱：增加檢索件數雖可能補回必要文件，也可能把更多無關內容交給語言模型。作者以兩組手工設定的常見問題排序，分別計算文件層級召回率與精確率；增加件數後，範例先找回漏掉的答案文件，之後只增加雜訊。另一段程式示範結合件數上限與分數門檻，並提醒高門檻也可能排除必要證據。實作上，應固定切塊與排序設定，使用同一組有標記的問題，分別追蹤取得文件、檢索指標與最終答案品質；多文件問題則需標出完整證據集合，並持續加入接近真實流量的案例。重要限制是：本文沒有真正執行檢索模型或生成答案，也沒有比較不同模型、語料或門檻的實驗，兩張圖只是概念插畫。因此，它展示的是可重現的教學運算，不能證明增加件數必然降低答案正確率。精確率可能隨新增文件的相關性而上升或下降，分數也不是正確性的保證。適合拿來建立診斷流程與小型測試，不宜當作新研究成果或通用參數設定。

llm_evaluation.rationale_zh: 這是一篇範圍內的日本入門文章，介紹語言模型幻覺與較安全的應用設計。它清楚區分生成與外部檢索，提醒提示及 RAG 無法消除全部錯誤，並建議在具後果的使用之前加入引用、輸出驗證與評估。這些教育訊息實用，但不是新方法或實驗成果。十四個文字例子及流程全屬示意，沒有測量模型、資料集、基準、錯誤率或緩解方法比較。下一個詞元預測的說法是簡化說明，並非完整幻覺因果理論，也不能證明模型的知識或意圖。輸出格式限制不應被理解為事實查核，文中也沒有評估引用正確性、檢索召回率或驗證器失敗。外部主要來源交叉核對支持訓練與評估誘因及不確定性也具有作用，但這些補充證據不算本文自己的研究。唯一內嵌卡片是公司首頁，並非技術文獻。現有文章足以完成評估；缺少研究證據不等於來源缺件。

primary_link.title: なぜAIは「もっともらしい嘘」をつくのか？ ハルシネーションを理解する

top5.summary: This Japanese introduction uses hypothetical examples involving a nonexistent JavaScript method, features attributed to a future year and company policies to explain how language models can produce fluent but false answers. Its key distinction is between generation, obtaining supporting information and verification. Asking a model not to guess is only one step; applications also need appropriate context, checkable sources and output validation. The article illustrates RAG as retrieving relevant documents before providing their contents to the model, while warning that retrieval may miss information, return incorrect sources or be misinterpreted. RAG therefore cannot guarantee the elimination of hallucinations. Flows that execute generated SQL directly or make payments immediately after a model determines an amount illustrate the danger of acting without verification. Read these examples before the six countermeasures and seven-point recap, and relate the principles to failure cases in your own application. All fourteen text examples are illustrative rather than experimental records. The article provides no model comparisons, dataset, error rates or effectiveness evaluation. Next-token prediction is only a simplified mechanism explanation: training and evaluation incentives, uncertainty and abstention also affect errors. Constraining output format is likewise not factual verification. The article is useful for understanding layered validation, but deployment still requires separate evaluation of whether citations support answers, whether retrieval is complete and when validators themselves fail.
top5.summary_zh: 這篇日本入門文章以不存在的 JavaScript 方法、未來年份功能及公司規章等假想例子，說明語言模型為何可能產生流暢卻不符合事實的回答。閱讀重點是把生成、取得根據與驗證分開：提示模型不要猜測只是其中一步，還要提供合適的背景資料、讓使用者能核對出處，並在應用程式端檢查輸出。文章以 RAG 展示先搜尋相關文件、再把內容交給模型回答的流程，同時提醒搜尋可能漏掉資料、找到錯誤來源，或被模型誤解，因此不能保證消除幻覺。生成 SQL 後直接執行、讓模型判定金額後直接付款，則是文中用來警示未經驗證就採取行動的流程。建議先讀這些例子，再看六項對策與七點摘要，將原則對應到自己的失敗案例。需要注意，十四個文字例子都不是實驗紀錄，本文沒有模型比較、資料集、錯誤率或措施效果評估。下一個詞元預測只是簡化機制說明，訓練與評估誘因、不確定性及選擇不作答也影響錯誤；限制輸出格式亦不等於查證事實。本文適合建立分層驗證的基本觀念，但實際部署仍須另外評估引用是否支持回答、檢索是否完整，以及驗證器本身何時失效。
